title: Plots, love letters and remedies: The medieval secrets being revealed by AI
facts: Researchers used machine learning to decode the 408-page-long Borg cipher manuscript stored in the Vatican library.
The Borg cipher was encoded using 34 obscure symbols alongside a few Roman letters.
Decoding the Borg cipher revealed thousands of historical medical treatments.
Approximately 1% of the material in archives and libraries around the world is fully or partially encrypted according to some estimates.
Cryptologist Cecile Pierrot and her colleagues took six months to decrypt a 500-year-old letter from Charles V.
A decrypted letter by Charles V revealed his fear of an assassination plot by an Italian mercenary warlord.
Professor Michelle Waldispühl and colleagues used the Transkribus AI platform to transcribe a 1637 secret letter by nobleman Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben.
Sigismund Heusner von Wandersleben used up to eight different symbols to represent the letter E in his encrypted 1637 letter.
The Descrypt project is developing an AI tool to turn handwritten historical texts with obscure symbols into machine-readable documents.
Beáta Megyesi and her team developed an AI system capable of directly deciphering simple replacement codes from photos of pages.
Researchers successfully tested a new AI transcription and decryption system on the 105-page Copiale cipher.
The Descrypt project researchers have compiled a database of mysterious cipher scripts from old archives.
The Descrypt project's archive collection includes 400 mysterious encrypted postcards from the late 1800s to early 1900s.
An AI chatbot-style tool developed by Beáta Megyesi's team combines transcription and decryption in a single step.
Beáta Megyesi's team's AI chatbot translated and decoded a 500-symbol extract from the Borg cipher in slightly over 29 minutes.
